ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in a square grid, it is known that the three vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are all on the grid points. What is the value of the tangent of $\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend CB to intersect the grid at D and connect AD as shown in the figure:\\
Then $\angle ADC = 45^\circ + 45^\circ = 90^\circ$,\\
$\because AD = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}$, $CD = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2} = 2\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the tangent of $\angle ACB = \frac{AD}{CD} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}} = \boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$;

raw_record.standard_answer: Extend $CB$ to intersect the grid at $D$ and connect $AD$ as shown in the figure. method.method_draft: Synthetic auxiliary-triangle route: From the grid diagram, note that A and B lie on the same horizontal grid line, C is one grid square up and one grid square right from B, and the line CB continues down-left through another grid point D. Extend CB past B to this grid point D, then join A to D. Read from the grid that AD moves 1 square horizontally and 1 square vertically, so AD = sqrt(2), while CD moves 2 squares horizontally and 2 squares vertically, so CD = 2sqrt(2). Also AD is a 45-degree diagonal in the opposite direction to CD, so AD perpendicular CD. Since D lies on line CB, angle ACB equals angle ACD in right triangle ACD. Therefore tan(angle ACB) = opposite/adjacent = AD/CD = 1/2.
